turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_supercon_train.csv: 300 real materials, columns `composition`
    (element fractions as a compact formula string) and `target` (the
    measured critical temperature Tc (K)).
  - b3_supercon_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE materials whose critical temperature
    Tc (K) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and `composition`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST critical
temperature Tc (K), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**What the training set tells us about high Tc:**

| Family in training set | Typical Tc |
|---|---|
| Elements/alloys (Rh, Ir–Mo, Nb–Ti, Pd–Te…) | < 10 K |
| Borocarbides (RNi₂B₂C), Chevrel, A15 (Nb₃Sn, V₃Si) | 3–20 K |
| Fe-based (BaFe₂As₂ doped, FeSe/Te, LaFeAsO, K–Fe–Se) | 5–55 K |
| Electron-doped 214 cuprates (Nd₁.₈₅Ce₀.₁₅CuO₄…) | 14–25 K |
| Hole-doped La₂₋ₓ(Sr,Ca,Ba)ₓCuO₄ | 25–45 K |
| Y/RE-123 near optimal doping | 80–93 K |
| Bi-2212 (optimal) | 84–94 K |
| Hg-1201, Tl-1201/2201 | 70–97 K |
| **3-CuO₂-layer phases (Bi-2223, Tl-1223/2223, Hg-1223, Cu/Tl-1234)** | **105–137 K** |

So the ranking rule extracted from the data is clear: **Tc rises with the number of adjacent CuO₂ layers (n ≈ 3–4) and is maximal for Hg-, Tl-, and Pb-doped Bi three-layer phases.** Everything non-cuprate in the pool (Re–Zr, Be–Ni, Ir–Os–Rh, Pd–H, Mo₆S₈, B₂Ta, MgB₁.₇₅C₀.₂₅, Fe-pnictides/chalcogenides, RNi₂B₂C) caps out well below 60 K.

**Screening the pool for n ≥ 3 layered cuprates:**

- **c084 Hg₀.₇Bi₀.₃Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈.₃₅** – Hg-1223 analogue; training's Hg₀.₉Pb₀.₁Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈.₂₅ = 118 K and Hg₁Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃F₀.₆O = 130 K → highest expected (~125–130 K).
- **c029 Ag₀.₂₅Cu₀.₇₅Ba₂Ca₃Cu₄O₁₁** – (Cu,Ag)-1234, four CuO₂ layers; cf. Cu₀.₅Tl₀.₅Ba₂Ca₁.₆Mg₀.₄Cu₃O₁₀ = 115 K → ~115–120 K.
- **c046 Bi₁.₇Pb₀.₂Mo₀.₁Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O** – Pb-doped Bi-2223; training analogues 106–111 K → ~108–112 K.
- **c097 Bi₁.₆Pb₀.₄Sr₂Ca₃Cu₄O (Ag trace)** – Pb-doped Bi-2223/2234 → ~105–110 K.
- **c034 Tl₂Ba₂Ca₅Cu₆O₁₆** – Tl-22(n) high-n member; Tl-2223 in training = 110 K, high-n members somewhat lower → ~105–110 K.
- Next best (just outside): c081 (Bi,Pb,V multilayer ~105 K), c072 (Bi-2212-like ~85 K), c076 (I-intercalated Bi-2212 ~80 K), then the many 123/2212 members at 80–93 K.

**Final: c084, c029, c046, c097, c034**
